- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to compensate for downward bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots in subsequent days; apply a “cool-down” correction: reduce forecast by 2–5% for 2–3 days post-spike.
- If model forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, consider mean reversion bias — adjust downward by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, if forecast is >10% above true outcome, check sentiment history: if sentiment is rising, model may be overconfident; if falling, model may be underestimating — adjust based on sentiment trend direction.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.00” (neutral or negative) followed by “1.00” (positive), model often fails to catch momentum — anticipate upward correction in next 3–5 days.
